name: OLALLA Water System
event_text: August 2024. The most recent BWN (issued April 24) is the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. In the report dated May 23, Total Coliform bacteria are present throughout the Distribution System, including the Storage Reservoir and No Total Coliform bacteria were reported from the source well. Based on the level of bacteria reported, the RDOS decided to reinstate the temporary chlorination. RDOS on-going efforts to determine the source of the contamination entering the system include: • Enhanced bacteriological sampling, • Extensive flushing of the distribution system, • Temporary chlorination (October 11, 2024 to February 18, 2025), • WQA (March 13 to 24), • BWN ISSUED APRIL 24, 2025, • Temporary chlorination (April 30 to May 9), • May 2, 2025, the RDOS hired a contractor with a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to inspect the inside of the storage Reservoir, and no apparent sources of contamination were noted from this inspection. • Temporary chlorination (May 23, 2025 to June 9, 2025), RDOS is now planning to isolate the storage Reservoir from the distribution system to further determine if the source of contamination is associated with the Reservoir. This will require some additional programming of the pump control system in advance to allow the system to modulate the speed of the Well Pump to continually maintain a set pressure in the distribution system while the Reservoir is isolated. Once this programming is complete, chlorination will again be removed from the system (scheduled for June 9) to allow for bacteriological testing. The Olalla System consists of a single deep source groundwater well, an elevated storage reservoir and distribution system. The water supply is typically not treated; the system is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System has approx. 200 service connections.

name: QUAMICHAN LAKE
event_text: QUAMICHAN LAKE (North Cowichan) – (WQA/BGA) June 27 Permanent Advisory has been in place for 10 years as a result of ongoing high bacteriological counts and frequent toxic algae blooms. Quamichan Lake has been subject to cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) since the 1930s. In the past two decades, the blooms have become longer and more intense. The root cause of these blooms is high concentration of phosphorus, which is largely due to excessive nutrient loading that has accumulated in the lake sediment over 150 years of runoff from forested, farmed and developed lands in the Quamichan watershed. Human activity since the turn of the last century has elevated nutrient levels in Quamichan Lake such that it is now considered a Highly Eutrophic Lake; dissolved oxygen has depleted to the point where the aquatic life begins to die off. Due to this predisposition, Island Health no longer tests the water and has a permanent advisory in place.

name: OLALLA Water System
event_text: MARCH 11, 2025 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system. JANUARY 20, 2026 - WQA remains in effect along with chlorination of the system. NOVEMBER 6, 2025 WQA in effect. Based on recent bacteriological results, the Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS), in consultation with Interior Health, have downgraded the Boil Water Notice (BWN) that has been in effect since April 24, 2025. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported since August 2024; the BWN was the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. The source of the contamination has yet to be determined in spite the substantial testing completed by the RDOS. As a result, the System will remain chlorinated for the foreseeable future. Currently, there is no treatment system in place for the groundwater (a single deep well), supplying the Water System. Typically, the System is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System serves approximately 250 connections. -- AUGUST 11, 2025 BWN remains in effect. This System remains under a Boil Water Notice as Regional District of Okanagan-Similkameen (RDOS) has yet to determine the source of contamination, despite their continued efforts. Most recent efforts involved: • The Reservoir was isolated, and the System was ran dynamically for the last few weeks. • The Reservoir was also emptied and disinfected while offline. • Further work to improve the water quality is anticipated to take place in the fall. • Additional measures will be implemented in the coming months to prevent backflow conditions within the System, and the reservoir is expected to be lined for further source protection. -- JUNE 27, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination has been reinstated. In continued efforts to determine the source of the contamination RDOS is now planning to change the configuration of the system and informs residents that the chlorination will be turned on and off for different periods of time. -- JUNE 9, 2025 BWN remains in effect and Temporary Chlorination will be suspended to facilitate further bacteriological testing as part of on-going efforts to pinpoint the source of the contamination. Total coliforms and background bacteria have been periodically reported in water system samples since August 2024. The most recent BWN (issued April 24) is the result of an increase in the frequency and quantity being reported. In the report dated May 23, Total Coliform bacteria are present throughout the Distribution System, including the Storage Reservoir and No Total Coliform bacteria were reported from the source well. Based on the level of bacteria reported, the RDOS decided to reinstate the temporary chlorination. RDOS on-going efforts to determine the source of the contamination entering the system include: • Enhanced bacteriological sampling, • Extensive flushing of the distribution system, • Temporary chlorination (October 11, 2024 to February 18, 2025), • WQA (March 13 to 24), • BWN ISSUED APRIL 24, 2025, • Temporary chlorination (April 30 to May 9), • May 2, 2025, the RDOS hired a contractor with a Remotely Operated Vehicle (ROV) to inspect the inside of the storage Reservoir, and no apparent sources of contamination were noted from this inspection. • Temporary chlorination (May 23, 2025 to June 9, 2025), RDOS is now planning to isolate the storage Reservoir from the distribution system to further determine if the source of contamination is associated with the Reservoir. This will require some additional programming of the pump control system in advance to allow the system to modulate the speed of the Well Pump to continually maintain a set pressure in the distribution system while the Reservoir is isolated. Once this programming is complete, chlorination will again be removed from the system (scheduled for June 9) to allow for bacteriological testing. The Olalla System consists of a single deep source groundwater well, an elevated storage reservoir and distribution system. The water supply is typically not treated; the system is monitored for potential contamination and undergoes periodic flushes and temporary chlorination as needed. This System has approx. 200 service connections.
